AML Compliance Review Checklist — Transaction Monitoring & CDD Assessment Q1 2026
■
Validate transaction monitoring rule coverage and mapping to
AML risk typologies (including newly onboarded product lines)
■
Test a representative sample of alerts for investigation quality
and disposition accuracy, including false-positive and
false-negative analysis
■
Back-test historical SAR cases against current monitoring
parameters to identify missed alerts and tuning needs
■
Review a random sample of customer due diligence (CDD)
files for completeness, risk rating accuracy, and documented
source-of-funds verification
■
Reconcile SAR filing statistics by typology and jurisdiction, and
identify trends in timeliness, filing quality, and supervisory
feedback
■
Assess the adequacy of enhanced due diligence (EDD)

■

thresholds by measuring alert volumes, escalation rates, and
investigator turnaround times
■

CDD process improvements, and case management workflow
enhancements
■
Prepare a summary of governance and senior management
reporting gaps, including KRI/KPI definition and reporting
cadence recommendations
■
Coordinate a training and implementation plan for investigators
and frontline staff to address identified quality gaps and new
monitoring rules

to 61.4% driven by a favourable product-mix shift. Operating expenses rose to $2.1M, primarily due to
headcount additions in engineering. Net income after tax was $890K, with EBITDA of $1.3M.

The organisation must achieve ISO 27001 certification by 2025-06-30 as required under the enterprise
customer contract signed on 2024-08-15. Gap analysis identified 34 controls requiring remediation, of
which 12 are rated critical. External assessor fees are estimated at $85,000. Failure to certify triggers a
contract penalty of $500,000.
AML Compliance Review Checklist — Transaction Monitoring, CDD & SAR Analysis (Q1 2026)
■
Test 200 sample transaction-monitoring alerts across high-risk
product lines to assess rule precision and false-positive rates
■
Compare detection rates for sanctioned jurisdictions against
the prior quarter to evaluate tuning impacts
■
Review 50 enhanced due diligence files for PEPs and high-risk
corporates for documentation completeness and risk rationale
■
Analyze SAR filing statistics by typology, customer segment,
and reporting lag to identify under-reported patterns and
timeliness issues
■
Reconcile transaction-monitoring system tuning logs with
change-control records to verify governance, approvals, and
implementation dates
■
Validate that customer risk-scoring model inputs are current
and re-run scores for a 5% customer sample to check score
accuracy
■
Assess the effectiveness of alert prioritization by measuring
analyst disposition times and escalation rates for high-severity
alerts
■
Update AML program recommendations with prioritized
enhancements from the review, including detection rule
changes, CDD improvements, and staffing adjustments
■
Prepare a SAR quality dashboard showing filing accuracy,
outcomes, supervisory feedback, and month-over-month
trends for management reporting
■
Document observed training gaps and draft targeted analyst
training modules to reduce false positives and improve CDD
assessments and SAR rationale
The Q4 planning meeting agreed that the product roadmap will be frozen after 2024-11-01 to allow
engineering to focus on delivery. Three features were deprioritised: advanced reporting, multi-tenant SSO,
and the AI recommendation engine. The CTO requested a technical feasibility review for the AI engine
before the next board presentation on 2024-12-10.

Customer Due Diligence Quality, Suspicious Activity Reporting Performance, and Programme
Enhancements (2024 Results)
On 15 February 2025, the Compliance Quality Assurance team completed a CDD QA review of 300
account files and identified a material deficiency rate of 18.0% (54 of 300). The deficiencies were
concentrated in outdated source-of-funds documentation, inadequate risk-scoring rationale, and
incomplete beneficial ownership verification for legal-entity customers. Findings indicate systemic
weaknesses in front-line collection and first-line supervisory sign-off. Remediation priorities include
immediate file cures for 54 identified accounts, additional targeted re-training for 150 onboarding officers,
and a six-week retrospective review of new client acceptances from Q4 2024 to identify gaps. The CDD
QA report was presented to Compliance Leadership on 20 February 2025.
In 2024 the Financial Crimes Reporting unit filed 1,246 suspicious activity reports (SARs), of which 312
were submitted within 30 days of initial detection, representing 25.0% timeliness. The remaining 75.0%
were subject to extended investigation timelines driven by complex cross-jurisdictional inquiries, additional
evidence collection, and enhanced due diligence on higher-risk entities. Internal review identified
case-management bottlenecks in evidence aggregation and legal review backlogs as primary contributors
to delayed filings. Immediate corrective steps recommended include strengthening case triage, expanding
the SAR investigation team by 12 full-time equivalents, and implementing a 30-day monitoring KPI with
weekly senior-management dashboards to improve adherence to statutory expectations.
The recommended programme roadmap establishes clear milestones to reduce the material CDD
deficiency rate from 18.0% to 10.0% by 30 September 2025. Key initiatives include: 1. policy refresh and
standardized CDD checklists by 31 March 2025; 2. phased deployment of automated document
verification and risk-scoring by 30 June 2025; 3. mandatory CDD certification for all relationship managers
with quarterly assessments; and 4. monthly QA cycles with rolling sampling of 200 files and remediation
SLAs. Progress will be tracked through a formal steering committee chaired by the Head of Compliance,
with baseline (30 June 2025) and final assessments tied to executive remuneration metrics.

Transaction Monitoring Effectiveness and Alert-to-Case Conversion (Q1 2024–Q1 2025)
In Q1 2025 the transaction monitoring system generated 48,620 alerts, an increase from 41,880 alerts in
Q4 2024. This 16.1% quarter-on-quarter rise strained analyst capacity and widened the review backlog
across Retail Banking and Commercial lines. The higher volume corresponded with product launches and
elevated cross-border flows in January and February 2025. Operationally, queue lengths and overtime
hours rose; the average daily intake in March 2025 exceeded capacity planning assumptions that were
calibrated to Q4 2024 volumes. The escalation in alerts necessitates immediate tuning and prioritisation to
maintain risk coverage without unsustainable resource increases.
The alert-to-case conversion rate fell from 7.8% in Q4 2024 to 6.1% in Q1 2025, indicating lower yield per
alert despite the higher volume. This decline suggests either an increase in false positives or that tuning
thresholds are no longer aligned with evolving customer behaviour and risk typologies. Compliance and
Line 1 partners should review rule-level performance and consider: 1. rebalancing threshold sensitivities;
2. retiring low-value alerts; and 3. implementing risk-scoring enhancements to prioritise high-probability
examinations. A data-driven re-tuning plan with defined acceptance criteria is required by end of Q2 2025
to restore conversion performance.
The median alert clearance time increased to 3.6 days in March 2025 from 2.4 days in December 2024,
reflecting backlog effects; remedial actions should include temporary analyst capacity, targeted automation
for low-risk alerts, and tightened SLA monitoring through April–June 2025 immediately.
